text:
{
  "status": "NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT",
  "SYSTEM_INTERPRETATION_OF_USER_INTENT": "The system treats past interactions as broad, continuing interest in related products or content, with insufficient attention to current purpose.",
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_RIGHT": [
    "Recommendations align when they extend a specific recent activity with a useful complementary item.",
    "Content recommendations align when they preserve a recurring theme, preferred artist, sound, or story quality."
  ],
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_WRONG": [
    "Broad category connections frequently displace closer matches to users' specific tasks or content preferences.",
    "Related products repeat capabilities or supplies users already have without establishing an unmet need.",
    "Older interests remain influential when recent interactions suggest a more specific current direction."
  ],
  "OVERUSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Shared category, ecosystem, or general activity is treated as sufficient evidence of relevance.",
    "Prior purchases and familiar artists or product families are treated as continuing demand without checking what makes another choice worthwhile."
  ],
  "UNDERUSED_OR_MISSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Recent sequences and repeated specific interests provide stronger intent clues than isolated historical interactions.",
    "Compatibility, dimensions, quantity, existing ownership, and complementary function determine whether related supplies are useful.",
    "Story tone, musical style, artist identity, and seasonal relevance distinguish compelling content from loosely related alternatives.",
    "Unidentifiable content leaves relevance uncertain and does not establish dislike or a reliable preference signal."
  ],
  "PRIMARY_FAILURE_MODE_AT_TOP_OF_LIST": "Too many leading recommendations offer broad resemblance without a specific reason to choose them now, crowding out items that match current interests or fill a practical gap.",
  "DIAGNOSTIC_SIGNALS_TO_TRACK": [
    "The share of leading recommendations users would choose, distinguishing concrete task or content connections from broad similarity.",
    "The frequency of skips attributed to duplicated capabilities, incompatible specifications, excessive quantities, or unsupported activities.",
    "Choice rates for recommendations aligned with recent repeated interests versus older isolated interactions.",
    "The frequency of uncertain judgments caused by unidentifiable content, tracked separately from explicit preference mismatches."
  ]
}
